_comment: Voice-over, one entry per video segment. {placeholders} are filled from docs/slides/deck_data.json.
title: Table for Two. Two robot arms set a dinner table from a single sentence, planned and driven on Intel OpenVINO.
plan: A small language model, running locally on OpenVINO, turns the instruction into a step-by-step plan. Before the robot moves, every plan is checked: the planner simulates what each hand is holding, so the arms never pour without the bottle.
demo: Nothing here is glued to a gripper. Every object moves only because the fingers squeeze it and friction holds it. The left arm pulls the drawer open by its handle while the right arm sets the mug down. The plate goes on the placemat and the fork beside it. The right arm grips the bottle from the side, tilts it over the mug, and the water, twenty-four small beads, pours in. Then the left arm turns the spoon and hands it across to the right.
grid: Robustness matters. Across ten held-out scenes we change object positions, masses, friction, lighting and the colour of the table, so a grasp that is too weak really does drop the object.
results: On the same ten scenes, the learned policy alone completes the whole task in {policy_full_task}, and in {hybrid_full_task} when a script finishes the stages it times out on. We report its weak spots as they are.
latency: On Intel hardware, NNCF INT8 quantisation runs the policy in {int8_cpu_ms} milliseconds on the CPU, {int8_speedup_words} faster than full precision.
closing: Grasps are real contact, stages finished by a script are never counted as policy wins, and everything you have seen is reproducible from our repository. Thank you.
